answer: The parchment maker soaks his skins in the lime vat behind the shop, and the vat is stirred every morning before the shutters open. Proof of parchment maker skin via lime soak record is the soaking: a sheet the maker lifts only after 9 days in lime, each day marked on the vat. The knoll is the first skin, lowered at dawn; the karst is the ninth, lifted when the hair slipped free. A cheat must soak 17 false skins and stir 17 false vats, and the haven still yields no sheet fit to write on.
